sections.title: What we're building
sections.text: Were designing a cozy isometric snowball fight game.  There are two teams, each team, has 4 players.  This is a single player game so I'm leaving it vague for you to decide.

sections.title: Decided (Foreman; host's calls outrank everything)
sections.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies (Pip, Scoop, Waffle) vs 4 AI. Match = first to 2 rounds of 120s (host): your hill, their hill, the park only at 1-1.
- Round: most crown-seconds with the toboggan. Sled starts beside the human in round 1, foot-centre in rounds 2–3. Every crown = same flat saddle. Tie → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Clock: afternoon → dusk (≥4 steps) → streetlights at 120s, plus a 20s countdown. Lighting resets between rounds.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot, whole ~26m hill, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.
- Controls (host): mouse only. Right-click walks toward the cursor, left-click throws (hands off while carrying), middle-click builds.
- No elimination: a chilled kid warms up at the cocoa stand, ~8s, out of play. Target ≤2 chills per kid per round (bench + siege chills counted together, <15%).
- Garage shop (host, rule 4): 4 credits per round guaranteed + hits + crown time; one purchase per visit; ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10; upgrades last the match only. Shop screen may use text. Not yet built: bazooka, igloo, fort.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Wall: one per kid, 1s plant at your feet, 8s cooldown (ghost footprint). Nothing built on the crown.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire.
- AI: Beanie, Pockets (blower), Brick (never throws), Copycat; fair-bot dodging.
- SIEGE: whoever holds the crown faces one shared volley, ONE release frame per cadence, never more than 4 live rings. Defenders 8m+ bracket the carrier's path; closer ones throw one direct shot. Cadence 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45s per street; street 3 adds a second blower.
- Session: up to 3 named streets (Maple Court, Ivy Terrace, The Summit Kids); nothing carries between streets.

NEXT: Systems builds the siege, reruns the bot log against the 'Host playtest 1' limits, then the host plays again.

sections.title: Hook: Snow Day (Creative v0)
sections.text:
Chestnut Street against three rival streets, three sledding hills each, and the streetlights are about to come on. Get the toboggan to the crown and hold it there longer than they do.
TONE: cozy = warm, silly, low stakes. Every upgrade is garage or kitchen junk: the launcher is a tennis-ball thrower, the rock is dirty plough ice, the bazooka is a cardboard-tube snow cannon. If it looks like a weapon ad, reskin it.
FIRST 30s: the whistle, sled 2–3m from your porch, everybody sprints. No tutorial; teach by racing.
LIGHT: the sky resets each round because it is the round clock, not the evening's.

sections.title: What a good throw feels like (Creative)
sections.text:
A snowball is a hard flat line (0.35s + 0.05s/m) arriving as the kid flinches; a free, watching kid at 6–10m is hit ≥60%. Reflex-dodging is NOT the skill.
1) The skill is the angle: a kid facing you sees it; one at your side, behind, or busy can't. A 30–45% match hit rate is healthy.
2) A plain ball NEVER clears a wall — walls are the reason to move. Only the blower (0.50s + 0.12s/m) arcs.
3) A miss looks like a near miss: it skids past the boots, ≥80% within 1.2m.

sections.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
sections.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match (first to 2 rounds of 120s, hill A, final camera, full dusk ending, porch screen). Temp audio on: whistle, crunch, sled shout, release, impact, wall break, lights clunk; no sound for a landing ring. No audio = void session.

WATCH, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s; 2) hands off in the first minute (QA #23); 3) builds unprompted in round 1, and whether a cooldown press stops them; 4) says who's winning at 35s and 105s; 5) porch button + hover time (QA #24); 6) what they look at while carrying (QA #25). Write down the first unprompted complaint verbatim, with the minute.
STOPWATCH: seconds the human can't act (chilled, walking, at the stand; carrying is play). Target <15%; >25% = bench or walk too long.
CSV: human's share of crown-seconds (QA #21); sudden-death rounds (>1 in 6 = scoring too flat); crown vs open-field chills.
AFTER: what told you time was running out (sky or countdown)? How did you know the sled changed hands? Lose sight of sled or kid? What changed the score? Best moment? What did you do when not carrying? Reopen the shop on purpose?

ONE FIX PER FAILURE, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, no text.
- never builds → cut the human's build; Brick keeps his walls.
- stops building after a cooldown press → bolder ghost footprint, no text.
- can't say who's winning → fix the score strip.
- loses the sled → camera or pennant failed; no new HUD.
- not in the score (QA #21) → move the round 2–3 sled toward Chestnut; never slow allies.
- picks 'Finish snow day' → don't shorten the clock. Bucket possession changes by 30s: mostly in the first 60s = fix crown/geometry; late = the ending failed.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

nodes.title: Snow Day whistle
nodes.notes: Everyone starts on their own porch. Round 1: sled 2–3m from the human's porch (the tutorial), plain snowballs only. Rounds 2–3: sled at the foot of the hill, centre, with whatever the garage sold. Everybody sprints.

nodes.title: Snowball exchange
nodes.notes: Carry the sled to the crown and hold it; the carrier is slow and unarmed, so teammates escort and wall the approach (middle-click). Holding the crown draws a siege volley. Hit = chilled (see Cocoa stand).

nodes.notes: Lights flicker on at 120s: most crown-seconds takes the round. Level = sudden death.

nodes.title: Porch screen → Garage shop
nodes.notes: Only while the match is still open. Porch screen: grudge line + round score, 'Continue'. Then the garage: one purchase per kid (rule 4); upgrades last the match. Then the next hill: yours, theirs, the park.

nodes.title: Sudden death (capped 60s)
nodes.notes: Per ROUND, not per match: if crown-seconds are level at the streetlights, sudden death. First team to hold the crown 5 continuous seconds; after 60s, the first crown-second wins. A match can never end tied.

nodes.title: Match end on the porch
nodes.notes: First team to 2 rounds wins. Porch screen: the grudge line + score, then 'Next street' / 'Finish snow day' (win or lose). After street 3: 'New snow day' / 'Finish snow day'.

nodes.title: Cocoa stand
nodes.notes: Side of the hill. Chilled kid walks over, warms up, jogs back: ~8s total. Out of play while there (not targetable, not counted). A dropped sled stays where it fell.

entries.label: Scoring
entries.text: 1 pt/sec while the sled is carried on the crown; most at 120s wins the round. Credits buy upgrades, never decide a round.
entries.author: user

entries.label: Porch screen: two lines, no stats
entries.text: Line 1 = the grudge, and it may name one kid ('Maple Court took your hill — Beanie got you twice' / 'Pip took it back'). Line 2 = the round score. Between rounds: 'Continue' to the garage; match end adds the street buttons (rule 10). The only place history and names appear.

objects.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems
objects.title: Core loop rules — Systems (numbers kept stable; 2 and 9 were cut)

entries.label: 1. Sled is carried, not camped
entries.text: Carrier: 60% speed, can't throw or build. No stealing: the sled changes hands only when a chilled carrier drops it in place (anyone may then pick it up) or by a handoff (rule 6). A dropped sled stops scoring until grabbed. Camping = slow, unarmed target, so teammates escort.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 2. Idle sled slides home
entries.text: Nobody touching the sled for 15s and it slides back to the bottom of the hill (kids shout). Score pauses. Kills the 0-0 turtle and forces someone to be the sucker.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 3. Sudden death
entries.text: Tie at the lights: first team to HOLD the crown 5 continuous s (a drop, chill or rival pickup resets to 0); after 60s the first crown-second wins. The cap never pauses.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 4. Garage shop + economy (4/8/10 price ladder)
entries.text:
Between rounds only; every kid shops, bots included; upgrades last the match. Round 1 = plain snowballs.
CREDITS: 1 per hit, 1 per 6 crown-seconds, 4 per round played, +2 per round win. No income cap; savings carry between rounds of the same match.
PRICES: ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10. Cheapest = 4 = a no-hit, no-crown round, so the shelf is never bare (QA #28).
GUARDS: ONE purchase per visit. STREET TIER = the street's row in rule 10 (cadence, rings, mix, reaction); rival purchases never change it. Spending never touches scoring.
BOT WISHLISTS (first affordable item, one per visit): Beanie ice → launcher → rock; Pockets melter → snowman (keeps the blower; his throws stay blower); Brick melter → ice; Copycat buys what the human just bought, else ice → launcher.
Carriers can't throw, so upgrades pay off through handoff: an escort economy.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 5. Builds: snow wall by default
entries.text: Middle-click plants ONE low wall (1.5m) at your feet, facing your aim. 1s plant (busy, can't dodge); planting again moves it. 8s cooldown after any plant or break. Blocks flat throws; ice and rock break it. A bought snowman replaces the wall (rule 7). Igloo and fort are host-approved structures, not built yet.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 6b. Free-sled claim — allies never rob the human
entries.text:
Chestnut's three allies never claim a free sled while the HUMAN is the nearest Chestnut kid to it, for the first 4s the sled is free. They don't stop or wait: they run to support (crown, flank, wall) exactly as normal, and Pip still beats you to every loose sled you are not closest to. After 4s free, or the moment you are not nearest, ordinary Beanie logic applies and someone grabs it.

WHY: the round-1 sled sits 2–3m from the porch, so Beanie logic alone decides the first possession before a first-timer's hands are even on the keys — exactly the spectator case QA #21 measures. This is a possession-assignment clause, not bot hesitation: no animation, nothing on screen, fair-bot rule untouched, and rivals are exempt (Maple's Beanie will still sprint at YOUR free sled). Fails safe: if human carry share is still under 1/3, move the sled start, never make the allies slower.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 6. One order = handoff
entries.text: While carrying, left-click shoves the sled to the one ally outlined within 6m (carrier types only, never Brick). Aimed elsewhere it does nothing — no toss, cooldown or sound — so a carry means walking. Teacher: an eligible ally within 6m with no ring on them waves for the sled. No text.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 7. Throwing: aim a spot, hard line
entries.text:
Mouse aims a landing ring (r 0.8m); left-click throws. Ring visible to all from commitment; ball casts a shadow dot. Your own ring hides while you carry; the handoff outline replaces it (QA #25).
- Plain: 0.35s + 0.05s/m, flat, 12m, NEVER clears a wall.
- Ice: 0.25s + 0.03s/m, flat, 12m, shatters the wall it hits.
- Rock: plain flight (0.35s + 0.05s/m, 12m) but smashes through walls and snowmen and keeps going; a kid it chills is knocked 1.5m off the spot, so a carrier lands away from the sled they dropped.
- Launcher: hold to spray pellets: 0.3s + 0.04s/m, 9m, ring 0.45m, scatter up to 0.5m, 15-ball hopper, 2.5s reload when empty. One pellet chills, same as a ball; balance it by price and the shop gate, not by a damage system.
- Melter: walking into a rival wall or snowman melts it; touching a chilled teammate thaws them instantly (once per 6s). Host's call: this restores the ruled-out 'heal a chilled ally' idea.
- Snowman: your build button makes a snowman instead of a wall (3 hits to break, 12s cooldown); it pelts rivals within 8m every 2.2s.
- Blower (Pockets): 0.50s + 0.12s/m, high lob, clears walls, 14m.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 8. Nothing gets built on the crown
entries.text: No walls inside the 4m crown circle or within 2m of the sled: no camping under cover.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 10. Session ladder — 3 streets, no carry-over
entries.text:
Nothing carries between matches. Snow day = up to 3 streets (~20 min). Plain rings come from Beanie and Copycat, blower cappers from Pockets; Brick never throws.
Street 1 (Maple Court): mix Beanie, Pockets, Brick, Copycat; siege 2.0s; 2 plain (lead + one side) + 1 capper; reaction 0.60s.
Street 2 (Ivy Terrace): same mix; 1.5s; same rings; 0.50s.
Street 3 (The Summit Kids): Beanie + 2 Pockets + Brick; 1.45s; 1 plain lead + 2 cappers covering both exits; 0.45s.
Cadence floor 1.45s (0.85s plain flight to 10m + 0.6s). Never more than 4 live rings (QA #29).
After each match: equal 'Next street' / 'Finish snow day'; after street 3: 'New snow day' / 'Finish snow day'. History only on the porch screen.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 11. Build numbers
entries.text:
One hit chills. Sled start: round 1 in the human's lane 2–3m from their porch; rounds 2–3 centre at the foot. Every crown = same flat 4m radius; only approaches change. Greybox reaction 0.50s (log header).
SPEEDS: kid 4.5 m/s, carrier 2.7 m/s, no stamina or slope modifier. A DODGE is not a separate move: it's walking out of a ring. From a standstill a 0.8m step takes ~0.25s at run speed (acceleration included). The human dodges the same way with right-click; there is no dodge button.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 12. Camera: one fixed iso shot
entries.text: Whole ~26m hill in one 1280×720 frame (~49px/m, kids ~48px). No follow or pan; human, sled, crown, both porches and flanks always visible. Same footprint on all three hills. Each porch at the foot of its side; kids emerge in a 1.2m arc, human front-centre.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: 13. Busy vs free stance
entries.text: BUSY (planting) can't move at all. A CARRIER can only walk at 2.7 m/s: 1.0m out of a ring in 0.37s, 2.0m in 0.74s. A FREE kid steps 0.8m in ~0.25s. That gap is why the siege bites and the bracket must come from range. The pose is the information.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

objects.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa
objects.title: QA: playtest risks — test these before adding anything

entries.label: 15. Outcomes read as aftermath — ACCEPTED
entries.text: Spec in Art 'Feedback'. TEST: unlabelled 60s clip, ask 'how many throws missed?' None = misses aren't rendering; hit vs untouched unclear = chill state too subtle.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 17. Cocoa stand out of play — ACCEPTED
entries.text: TEST: log repeat-chills within 5s of returning; more than a couple = the stand is exposed, move it further off the hill.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 21. Is the human actually in the score?
entries.text: Pip and Scoop can win without the human. CSV: crown-seconds per carrier. Share <1/3 is calibration, not a gate. FAIL only if share <1/3 AND, asked 'what changed the score?', they name only an ally's carry. FIX: move the round 2–3 sled 1.5m toward Chestnut; never slow allies.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 23. Handoff: count silent presses
entries.text: A failed handoff is silent, so 'too far' and 'nobody eligible' look alike. From the input log, count carrying throw-presses with no handoff before the first success, per round. 1–2 = the wave taught it; 3+ = fix the wave (ally turns, arm higher), never a ring, number or tooltip; zero = 'never hands off'.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 24. 'Next street' is the verdict — log the button
entries.text: Log the button and hover seconds. Next fast = wants more; hovering Next ~10s then Finish = a cost not worth paying; Finish instantly = done. No prompting; Next never styled nicer than Finish.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 25. Aim ring hidden while carrying — ACCEPTED (rule 7)
entries.text: TEST: ask 'what were you looking at while carrying?' and 'how did you know where the rings would land?' Watching their own cursor = the ring is stealing the siege read.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 26. Shop limits — ACCEPTED
entries.text: 1) Spend between rounds only. 2) One purchase per visit, or the tour becomes a grind. 3) No unlocks across snow days, or 'Finish snow day' starts to cost something. TEST: does any first-timer reopen the shop unprompted? If not, it's a screen, not a system: cut prices, keep two items.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 28. Shop beginner fix — RULED
entries.text: Cheapest item = 4 = what a no-hit, no-crown round pays, so the shop is never a locked door. Text allowed on the shop screen (host). TEST: ask 'what could you afford?'; counting aloud twice = the screen isn't reading.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 29. Max live rings — RULED: hard cap 4
entries.text: A volley is held back if releasing it would put more than 4 siege rings in flight on one carrier (e.g. 2 plain + 2 cappers). CSV logs max live rings per carrier per round to confirm.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 30. Melter and snowman — RULED: keep (host's picks), behaviour now in rule 7
entries.text: Not cut: the host chose both and they're built. One line each added to rule 7, matching greybox/src/sim/const.ts. Each still faces the shop-phase win-rate gate.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 31. Siege vs bench — RULED: one combined number; if bench >15% with holds at 8–20s, cut warm-up 8s → 5s first
entries.text: A chill costs ~8s, so <15% allows two chills per round; a willing carrier's 2–3 holds can blow that while the crown works fine. REPORT human chills + bench seconds as one number, not split by source. Bench >15% with holds at 8–20s: cut warm-up 8s → 5s first, move the stand second. Never shorten cadence for a bench number.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 48px identity — one rig, four variants
entries.text: One rig, four head/coat silhouettes reused by both teams. Priority: head shape, team colour + scarf pattern, pose. Chestnut = burnt orange bands; Maple = deep teal V. White overhead chevron = human only. Busy state from real carry/plant poses, no icon. Pennant on the sled, stays with a dropped sled. Charm goes in snowbanks and porch lights, not 48px detail.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Throw readout
entries.text: Plain: short bright streak, dark underside, moving shadow; never a lob. Blower: raised ball, broken coral touchdown bracket. Preview stops at walls; footprint matches collision. A miss skids past the boots and rests on the snow. No more warning layers before human testing.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Score strip + ownership
entries.text: Pennant = carrier's team; dropped = white. Crown edge pulses each scoring second. Top strip: teams, crown-seconds, sled icon by the scorer, exact countdown in the last 20s; dusk and lamps reinforce it. Handoff preview outlines ONE eligible ally within 6m with a short sled arrow; never Brick.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Greybox readability gate (human eyes, not telemetry)
entries.text:
Hill A, 1280×720, three unlabelled 1s clips (8-kid scrum / lob / wall interception) at sunset and dusk. A first-timer names human, carrier, leading team and incoming threat, then points to an escape; record errors and time.
FLANK: from each porch they point at the flank route within 1s, at dusk too.
MEASURE: kids ≥48px; landing footprint in projection; misses ≤1.2m for ≥80% (world-space CSV). The capture beats arithmetic.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Feedback: aftermath + wall status
entries.text:
HIT: chilled, stopped kid + brief puff. MISS: ball resting at the end of its skid. WALL BLOCK: lasting dent, not a hole; only ice/rock break walls. Never hide chevron or pennant; no clouds or screen shake.
WALL STATUS: ghost footprint fills with the cooldown, full outline when ready, barred when illegal; never looks solid. The plant pose starts only on a legal plant.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

objects.title: The eight kids — AI as characters

entries.label: Beanie — always wants the sled
entries.text: Makes the crown a door anyone can kick open. Silhouette: striped beanie.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Pockets — keeps 6m away (leaf blower)
entries.text: Back-line lobber; teaches you to respect the landing ring. Silhouette: bulging pockets.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Brick — only builds
entries.text: Walls the approach so his team's carry is easy. Silent, calm, faintly comic. Silhouette: too-big mittens, sits low.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Copycat — copies your action, never your allegiance
entries.text: Mirrors your last action type with an exaggerated version of your throw pose. Keeps Maple's teal scarf and his own hat: head shape is the top identity cue (Art), so he never borrows yours.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Chestnut's three — your street
entries.text: Pip (Beanie logic), Scoop (Pockets), Waffle (Brick). Same rig, orange bands, no new mechanics; the names make it 'my street'.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Names, not dialogue
entries.text: Learned by behaviour; a name appears only in the porch screen's grudge line. No barks or text in flow: cozy = quiet.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Behaviour rules (Systems) — no state trees
entries.text:
Beanie: grabs a free sled, shortest legal path to the crown. Throws only when the sled has been off the crown 5s+. Never builds.
Pockets: blower only; holds 6–10m from the nearest enemy, faces their carrier, backs off inside 6m. Carries only as fallback.
Brick: never carries, receives or throws. Keeps his wall between his carrier and the nearest threat (outside the crown, ≥2m from the sled); wall down = walks 2m ahead as a shield.
Copycat: 2s after the human acts, repeats that action type; never initiates (copies the stand-in in bot runs).
SIEGE suspends Beanie's 5s rule and Copycat's never-initiate rule (Host playtest 1).
FAIR-BOT: reacts only to committed rings in its ~120° front arc, after its reaction time, by walking 0.8m out (rule 11). Carriers and builders don't dodge.
Difficulty = street tier (rule 10); reaction 0.45–0.60s governs dodging only. Fallback carrier when Beanie is chilled 3s+: Pockets, then Copycat.
ALLIES: same logic. They never take a handoff the human didn't give, but a sled the human drops is free for anyone, allies included (6b stays ruled out).
SHOPPING: wishlists in rule 4.
STAND-IN (bot runs): Beanie logic, plain snowballs; in shop tests buys the item under test.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

objects.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems
objects.title: Greybox bot round — logs and pass/fail (Systems)

entries.label: Record one CSV, one fixed seed
entries.text:
Per second: sled state, both scores. Per throw: thrower, item, distance, ring position, flight time, outcome (hit / wall / empty / stepped out), target facing and busy. Per volley: shared release-frame ID (verifies one release per cadence). Per miss: closest approach. Per kid: chills, credits, purchases. Per round, 30s buckets: possession changes and handoffs, separately.
Conditions: hill A, 8 bots at 0.50s (stand-in in the human slot), all bots shopped to their street tier.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Pass/fail — does the loop exist
entries.text: Sled on the crown 25–60% of the round; ≥6 possession changes per round; longest hold ≤25s, else camping: fix geometry or a rule, never HUD. Log siege volleys (count, rings, hits).
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Pass/fail — are the decisions real
entries.text:
Clear a ring = reaction + 0.25s step + 0.1s slop (0.95 / 0.85 / 0.80s by street).
Free, facing kid at 6–10m: hit ≥60% (<50% = flight time wrong). Busy or flanked: ~100%.
Match hit rate 30–45%: >60% = bots blind; <25% = no flank route, fix geometry.
Chills: 4–8 per team per round, ≤2 per kid (2 × 8s = 13% of 120s); a 3rd is a geometry/spawn report. Count crown-hold chills apart from open-field.
Misses: ≥80% within 1.2m; a ball through a body is a collision bug.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Shop phase: per-item win rate, one retune then delete
entries.text: Per item: 30+ matches (0.50s, hill A) with the stand-in forced to buy it, vs plain-snowball control on the same seeds. Outside 40–60% win rate: one retune (price first), then cut. Launcher is the first suspect.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Wall-block share
entries.text: Share of plain throws that die on a wall. <25%: ship. 25–35%: watch, shorten the flank. >35%: walls are the game; fix geometry (wider flank) or a slower rebuild, not a new card.

objects.author: claude
objects.title: Host playtest 1: the crown is too safe (Systems, implement)

entries.label: Diagnosis (from greybox/src/sim/ai.ts)
entries.text: Against a human on the crown only Pockets attacked (one blower per 8s, easy to walk out of). Beanie waits for a drop, Copycat mirrors throws a carrier can't make, Brick never throws: 3 of 4 rivals passive exactly when the human scores.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Fix 1: Siege — one shared volley, not per-bot cadences
entries.text:
TRIGGER: an enemy carries the sled within 2m of the crown edge. Siege lasts until the sled is dropped, carried 2m+ away, or picked up by the defenders after a drop.
Every free defender (not chilled, carrying or planting) joins ONE shared volley timer, so each volley is one visible event. Siege suspends Beanie's 5s and Copycat's never-initiate rules for volley throws only. Brick still never throws.
SYMMETRIC: Pip/Scoop/Waffle siege a rival carrier the same way, so escorting matters both ways.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead from range, one direct shot up close, one release frame
entries.text:
One volley = every free thrower's ring on the SAME frame (rule 10 lists them per street).
FAR (8m+) plain rings: lead = carrier position + velocity × flight time; a second plain ring sits 1.2m to one side of the lead.
NEAR (<8m): one direct shot at the carrier's position, no lead, same frame.
CAPPERS (Pockets' blowers) land ~1s late on the obvious exit; on street 3 two cappers cover both exits.
The bracket punishes running straight, the near shot punishes standing still, the capper punishes the obvious exit. Irregular walking is the skill. Walking out of a ring inside the 4m crown keeps you scoring.
Handoff is the free escape: the volley lands where the sled was. All rings visible from release, no homing.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Fix 3: cadence floor 1.45s; the ramp is cappers
entries.text:
Floor = 0.85s plain flight + 0.6s = 1.45s; a capper may still be airborne at the next release. The street ramp is cadence (2.0 → 1.5 → 1.45s) then capper count (1 → 2 on street 3). Never more than 4 live rings.
Retune one lever at a time: capper count → cadence (1.45–2.0s) → lateral spacing (1.2m). Never shrink the 0.8m ring.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Gate (don't overcorrect)
entries.text:
Loop gates still hold. NEW: a willing carrier's median crown hold on street 1 is 8–20s (≥12 holds over 6 rounds), and no carrier is chilled by two volleys in a row more than twice per round. Log thrower distance on every siege ring: most crown chills from <8m = the near-range rule isn't implemented.
Never survives 8s → lengthen the volley period. Crown never held → fix geometry (cover outside the crown or a 2m no-throw band). Holds past 20s → add a capper before shortening cadence.
